title: Work authorisation and warehouse operating boundaries
audience: Cleaners and supervisors starting work in an operating warehouse.
learningOutcomes: Confirm the written work authorisation and the named supervisor before entering a warehouse work zone.
Identify the operating boundaries: traffic routes, dock areas, racking, plant and restricted zones.
Stop and refer when the authorisation does not match what is observed on site.

instruction.heading: Authority before entry
instruction.body: An operating warehouse is a busy workplace with vehicles, plant and stored goods moving around, and the work of the people on site depends on the routes and zones being used as planned. A cleaner who enters a zone without the site's authority can block a route, stand in a path of moving plant, or disturb stock that someone else is counting or loading. Before you enter a work zone, confirm four things: the written work authorisation, the named supervisor, the agreed zone and the time window. A cleaning booking is not an authorisation to enter a zone that the site has closed or reassigned. The booking records what someone asked for, and the authorisation records what the site has agreed to. If the two differ, the authorisation governs. Keep a copy of the authorisation with you while you work, or have the supervisor's contact available, so that you can show it on request.

instruction.heading: Site induction and the traffic plan
instruction.body: A site induction is the point at which the site explains its own rules to people who are new to it, and it is where the traffic plan is explained. The Safe Work Australia guidance on warehouse traffic management says that the plan should document how traffic risks are managed, and that it may include designated vehicle travel paths, the entry and exit points, crossing points, pedestrian routes, how often plant and people interact, the traffic controls for each expected interaction, and the responsibilities of the people who manage traffic. The guidance also says that workers and contractors must know and understand the traffic rules and procedures, and that site induction should cover the plan. Ask for the induction and the plan before the first entry, and do not rely on a plan you were given when the booking was made. If you have not been inducted, you are not authorised to enter a zone where plant moves, and the induction is the first step, not the cleaning.

instruction.heading: Operating boundaries on the site plan
instruction.body: Identify the boundaries on the site plan before you start: traffic routes, pedestrian walkways, dock areas, racking, plant and restricted zones. Mark anything that is not in scope. Traffic routes are the paths that vehicles use, including the aisles where forklifts run and the lanes at a dock. Walkways are the paths that people are meant to use, and they should be separate from routes, where the site can make them so. Dock areas include the edges, the leveller plates, the trailers and the door openings, all of which can move without warning. Racking is storage structure, and it is not part of the cleaning scope unless the site says so. Plant includes any machine that moves or lifts, and restricted zones include areas closed for maintenance, for hazardous storage, for testing or for another contractor. Do not enter a restricted zone to check whether it is clear, and do not cross a traffic route without the site's control. A zone that looks empty may be waiting for a vehicle, a load or a repair.

instruction.heading: When the site has changed
instruction.body: If the zone looks different from the plan, or the operations have moved, stop and check with the supervisor before you go on. A delivery may have arrived early, a pallet may be standing in an aisle, a barrier may have been moved, or a bay may have been reassigned for the day. Record the difference, the time and who you told. The authorisation follows the site's current plan, not the plan you were given at booking, so a change on the ground means the old plan no longer applies until the supervisor says it does. Do not decide that a change is minor, and do not work around it because the rest of the zone is open. The supervisor decides whether the zone is still in scope, and that decision is written down before you resume. A change that is reported and recorded is a normal part of the job, and a change that is not reported is the point at which an incident begins.

instruction.heading: Licences, plant and what this lesson does not authorise
instruction.body: Operating a forklift is one of the activities that Safe Work Australia's guidance on high-risk work licences lists as needing a licence. That guidance states that workers must have a licence before undertaking high-risk work, and it lists forklift trucks among the work covered. This lesson does not teach you to operate plant, and it does not grant a licence, a plant authority or a site authority. Do not move a pallet, climb onto a dock edge, use a plant attachment, or drive any vehicle to get a cleaning tool into place. Ask the site for a plant operator to move anything that is in the way, and wait.

procedure: Confirm the written work authorisation, the named supervisor, the zone and the time window before you enter.
Check that the site induction has been completed, and that the current traffic plan has been explained.
Mark traffic routes, walkways, dock areas, racking, plant and restricted zones on the current site plan.
Do not enter a restricted zone, and do not cross a traffic route without the site's controlled crossing.
Stop and check with the supervisor where the zone differs from the plan, and wait for a written decision.
Record the difference, the time and the person told, and resume only in the zone the supervisor has confirmed.
Ask a plant operator to move any load or equipment that blocks the work, and do not move it yourself.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner arrives for a booked clean, but the bay has been reassigned to a delivery and the current plan shows it as closed.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do, and how is the booking handled?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not enter the bay. The authorisation follows the current plan, and the bay is closed. Record the difference and the time, and tell the supervisor. Do not clean from the doorway, because the doorway may be in the path of the delivery. Ask the site to reschedule the work, and do not treat the booking as a reason to enter. The job waits for a written decision that names the bay.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor who is not the named supervisor on the authorisation waves you into a dock area to clean the edge of a leveller plate while a trailer is being unloaded.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you go in, and what is recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not go in. The named supervisor is the person who authorised the zone, and the dock area is an active zone with plant and moving loads. Record the request, the time, the person who asked, and the reason you did not enter. Ask the named supervisor to confirm the zone in writing before work resumes.

workedExamples.situation: The site plan shows an aisle as open, but the aisle is blocked by a pallet and a rack of stock is being counted at the far end.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the boundary, and what do you do?
workedExamples.reasoning: The plan does not match what you see, so the change governs. Stay outside the aisle, do not move the pallet, and do not step around it. Record the blockage, the stock count and the time. Tell the supervisor, and ask for a decision on whether the aisle is in scope. The cleaning of the aisle waits until the supervisor confirms it, and any clearing of the pallet is a job for the site's own staff.

equipmentAndPpe: Current site plan showing traffic routes, walkways, dock areas, racking, plant and restricted zones.
Written work authorisation with the named supervisor, the zone and the time window.
Site induction record and the current traffic plan, or a note of where the plan is kept.
High-visibility clothing and safety footwear as the site requires for the zone.

Personal protective equipment is a last resort after the boundary and the authorisation have been checked. Safe Work Australia describes personal protective equipment as one of the least effective controls, to be used after higher-level controls such as keeping clear.

commonErrors.error: Entering a bay because the booking says so.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the current plan and the written authorisation. The booking is not the authorisation.

commonErrors.error: Crossing a traffic route to save time, or stepping around a pallet in a route.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the site's controlled crossing, and ask the supervisor for a revised route if none exists.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a quiet zone is open because no one is working in it.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm with the supervisor. A quiet zone may be waiting for a load or a repair.

commonErrors.error: Accepting an instruction from someone who is not the named supervisor on the authorisation.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the authorisation. Confirm any change with the named supervisor, in writing where possible.

commonErrors.error: Moving a pallet, a barrier or a cart to clear a path for the cleaning equipment.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask a plant operator or the site's staff to move it. Do not move it yourself.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Safe Work Australia's guidance on warehouse traffic management says that the person conducting the business or undertaking must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that workers and others are not exposed to traffic risks, and must provide the information, training, instruction and supervision needed to do that. The guidance also says that those who manage the workplace must ensure that loadshifting equipment operators are trained and licensed. These are the site's duties, and this lesson does not transfer them to a cleaner.

Safe Work Australia's guidance on high-risk work licences states that workers must have a licence before undertaking high-risk work, and lists operating a forklift truck among that work. Cleaning does not include operating or moving plant, and this lesson does not grant any licence or plant authority.
The Safe Work Australia guidance is a national reference and is not a substitute for the law in the state or territory where the site is located.

This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist. A site authorisation for a zone does not come from this lesson, and only the site can give it.

qualityStandard: Written authorisation, named supervisor, zone and time window confirmed before entry in the desk exercise.
Operating boundaries marked on the current site plan, including restricted zones, in the case study.
Closed or changed zone not entered, with the difference recorded and the supervisor told, in the case study.
Resumption only in the zone the supervisor has confirmed in writing.
documentationEvidence: Authorisation check record, with the supervisor, the zone, the time window and the date.
Annotated site plan showing the operating boundaries.
Difference and supervisor-notification record, with the time and the person told.
Written decision from the supervisor on any changed zone before resumption.
summary: Confirm the written authorisation and the named supervisor before entering any zone.
Respect the operating boundaries on the current plan, and treat restricted zones as closed.
Stop and check with the supervisor when the site differs from the plan.
Do not operate plant or move loads; ask the site to do so.

knowledgeChecks.question: A bay is closed on the current plan, but your booking says it is open. What is correct?
options: Enter, because the booking is valid and the time has been set
Clean from the doorway, since the bay is not really closed
Do not enter; record the difference and tell the supervisor

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be used to cross a traffic route?
options: Any gap in the moving traffic
A quick run past the forklift

knowledgeChecks.question: What is a cleaning booking?
options: An authorisation to enter any zone of the site during the shift
A record of what was requested, and not an authorisation by itself
A permit to operate plant and move the racking equipment

knowledgeChecks.question: A pallet blocks an aisle the plan shows as open. What do you do?
options: Move the pallet so the aisle is clear, then carry on with the clean
Step around it and clean the far end of the aisle first before the rest
Stay outside, record the blockage, and ask the supervisor for a decision
